Your baby can taste more than you can. Babies are born with about 10,000 taste buds, nearly double w

Your baby can taste more than you can. Babies are born with about 10,000 taste buds, nearly double what adults have. They are everywhere - tongue, roof of mouth, even the back of the throat. No wonder they are so picky. #BabyFacts #Shorts #BabyScience #ParentingTips

Medicine moved the survival line by 6 weeks in one generation 👶

Medicine moved the survival line by 6 weeks in one generation 👶

In 1990, 28 weeks was the viability threshold for premature babies.

Today: 22-week preemies survive. Some as young as 21 weeks.

Modern NICUs have rewritten what's possible for the tiniest humans.

#babyfacts #premature #nicu #medicine #amazingfacts

Babies hiccup in the womb at 9 weeks 🤰 Long before they take their first breath, fetuses are already practicing. Womb hiccups train the diaphragm muscles needed for breathing. Your baby was getting ready for life — before they even had a face. #babyfacts #pregnancy #fetaldevelopment #womblife #amazingfacts
Newborns can swim. The dive reflex makes them hold their breath underwater. Gone by 6 months #BabyFacts

Babies copy your face before they can see clearly 👁️ Newborns mimic facial expressions within 42 minutes of birth. They can't see clearly. They've never seen a face before. Yet they stick out their tongue when you do. They open their mouth. They mirror. #babyfacts #mirrorneurons #newborn #babydevelopment #amazingbrain

Your baby knew your smell before they knew your face 👃 Within 1 hour of birth, newborns can identify their mother's scent. Put a cloth with mom's scent next to a stranger's — babies turn toward mom 80% of the time. They can barely see. But they already know you. #babyfacts #newborn #motherhood #amazingfacts #babydevelopment
A newborn's grip is so strong it can support its own body weight 💪👶 #BabyFacts #BabyStrength #MindBlown

Your newborn was born knowing how to swim. Kind of. It's called the dive reflex - when submerged, ba

Your newborn was born knowing how to swim. Kind of. It's called the dive reflex - when submerged, babies instinctively hold their breath and move their arms and legs. This reflex disappears around 6 months. #BabyFacts #Shorts #BabyScience #NewbornReflex
